2) Redwood provides a scoped pilot quote for the top two model configs.
3) If acceptable, we schedule a 2-week pilot with canary routing + monitoring.

I've attached: acme_model_shortlist.pdf (shortlist + rationale), acme_benchmark_results.csv (baseline internal numbers on similar workloads), and acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (recommended prompt set for evals). Also linking the benchmark folder here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_acme-benchmarks

If that plan looks good, can you confirm the sample dataset and your preferred pilot start window (next week or week after)?

Thanks 

Alicia 

Appreciate the clarity on priorities. Below is a concise recommended shortlist (3 configs) with rationale focused on cost/latency/quality tradeoffs and what we recommend for pilot vs production.

Recommended shortlist (pilot-first):

1) Redwood-Edge-7B-q4 (pilot)
- Rationale: quantized 7B provides the lowest per-token cost and sub-200ms P95 on our 16GB GPU staging for typical short prompts. Good for conversational FAQ where brevity is acceptable.
- Cost estimate: ~$0.0009 - $0.0012 per token (pilot volumes).
- Quality: solid instruction following for template-based help responses; may struggle on rare long-context factual retrieval.
- Use-case fit: initial pilot to validate latency profile and monitoring pipelines.

2) Redwood-13B-8k-q4 (canary -> production)
- Rationale: a middle ground that materially improves answer quality and factuality while keeping P95 ~220-300ms depending on batch settings. Offers best tradeoff for ACME's product constraints.
- Cost estimate: ~$0.0018 - $0.0022 per token.
- Quality: noticeably better on multi-sentence answers and instruction following.
- Use-case fit: recommended canary route for production if pilot latency checks out.

3) Redwood-30B-extended (evaluation only)
- Rationale: highest quality; recommended only for narrow supervised tasks or escalation flows due to cost/latency.
- Cost estimate: ~$0.004+ per token; P95 will be higher and may exceed your latency SLO without additional infra.
- Use-case fit: fallback/rare escalations where quality is critical.

Benchmarks & prompts:
- Internal CSV attached (acme_benchmark_results.csv) includes P50/P95 numbers across typical prompt lengths.
- Prompt set: acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (use these during the 72-hour eval to generate comparable metrics).

Compliance & procurement:
- Aditya will attach SOC 2 Type II and our onboarding checklist in the pilot packet. For procurement, if you can share the expected contract timeline we can align resources.

Next steps (suggested):
1) Confirm the sample dataset and pilot start window (we can start as early as Aug 24).
2) Redwood runs a 72-hour eval with Redwood-Edge-7B-q4 and Redwood-13B-8k-q4 against your sample.
3) We present final numbers + pilot quote and align on production cutover plan.

If this looks good I can put together the pilot packet and a proposed SOW.

Best,
Marissa
